# Functionality matrix

What libSACM implements, requirement by requirement. The canonical source is [`functionality-matrix.toml`](functionality-matrix.toml); the row format, status vocabulary and gate rules are described in [README.md](README.md). `SACM23-*` rows are obligations of the OMG SACM 2.3 standard; `LIB-*` rows are library capabilities and quality commitments.

Workspace, CI gates, matrix gate, reference fetching and agent guard are in place and verified, so every later slice runs on trusted tooling.

| SACM23-BASE-001 | **LangString.** LangString (§8.3) is a value type with an optional `lang` and an optional `content`, each a String [0..1]. For each field, absent, empty and non-empty are distinct (ADR 0012), and values are kept byte for byte: no trimming, case folding, Unicode normalisation or format check on `lang`. It is not a SACMElement: it has no id and no ElementKind. | SACM23-XMI-001 | **Interchange roots.** `xmi::read` returns `Ok(ReadOutput)` with a `Document` (and its diagnostics, sorted per ADR 0011: SACM-XMI-010 for `xsi:type` and SACM-XMI-011 for `xmi:version` (LIB-COMPAT-001), the Infos SACM-XMI-004 for a missing `xmi:id` and SACM-ID-004 for a padded one (SACM23-XMI-020, SACM23-XMI-025), and SACM-XMI-003 for preserved content (LIB-COMPAT-003), SACM-XMI-012 and SACM-XMI-013 for shapes and spellings a tolerant read reads (LIB-COMPAT-008, SACM23-XMI-009)) when every interchange root is an element of one of the twelve package kinds (the four packages, their interfaces and their bindings) in the pinned SACM namespace `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/20220301` (D-NS-PIN). A root is the document element, or each element child outside the XMI namespace of an `XMI` element in the XMI 2.5.1 namespace `http://www.omg.org/spec/XMI/20131001`. Elements and attributes are matched by namespace URI and local name, never by prefix (any-prefix equivalence is SACM23-XMI-002). Each root becomes a parentless element of its kind, in document order, whose id is its `xmi:id`'s `xsd:ID` value (SACM23-XMI-025), or a generated id when it has none (SACM23-XMI-020). Its name is missing (ADR 0013) unless it has a `name` child, which SACM23-XMI-012 reads. A read root may carry only namespace declarations, `xmi:id`, `xmi:version` (reported as SACM-XMI-011 and otherwise ignored: XMI 2.5.1 identifies its version by namespace) and an `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` naming its own class; its content may be only white space, comments, processing instructions, one `name` child under SACM23-XMI-012's rules, and the children SACM23-XMI-016 reads; content that does not conform there is preserved (below). The wrapper may carry only namespace declarations and `xmi:version`. An empty root id is `ReadError::InvalidId` and a root id that repeats an earlier element's is `ReadError::DuplicateId` (SACM23-VAL-020, SACM23-VAL-001). Content of a root that does not conform where it stands (an attribute or child element its class lacks, a type attribute naming another class (D-ROOT-NAME), an `id` attribute in no namespace or another namespace, non-white-space text) is kept as preserved content of the root, with one SACM-XMI-003 at it (Warning tolerant, Error strict; LIB-COMPAT-003, ADR 0033). Anything else is refused as `ReadError::Unsupported` at its location, never dropped (LIB-API-009, LIB-API-011): conforming content not read yet (XMI metadata and `xsi:schemaLocation` on a root, SACM23-XMI-019), a preserved attribute whose prefix binds `sacm` or `xmi` to another URI (a defect, ADR 0033), any attribute other than namespace declarations and `xmi:version`, and any non-white-space text, on the wrapper, a package-kind name in a SACM 2.4 namespace (LIB-COMPAT-018), or, in strict mode, in another SACM namespace (LIB-COMPAT-004), an `XMI` element in another namespace (LIB-COMPAT-002), and an XMI-namespace element as a root or wrapper child (SACM23-XMI-019). A root or wrapper child whose local name is none of the twelve package-kind names, one in no namespace or in a namespace whose URI does not contain `sacm` in any letter case, and a wrapper with no root, are refused with a `ReadError` whose `code()` is SACM-XMI-001, at that element; among the refusals found while reading the roots this takes precedence over `Unsupported`, so which roots get SACM-XMI-001 does not depend on what a release can read (an `XMI` element outside the XMI namespace is `Unsupported` before its children are classified, ADR 0016 D1). No document is returned beside a refusal (ADR 0015). | SACM23-XMI-002 | **Namespace-prefix independence.** `xmi::read` matches element and attribute names by expanded name (namespace URI and local name), and resolves the QName value of `xmi:type`/`xsi:type` against the namespaces in scope on the element that carries it, so the choice of prefix never changes the result, except that preserved content keeps its prefixes (LIB-COMPAT-003; a kept type value's prefix may be renamed on write, LIB-COMPAT-019). A document that SACM23-XMI-001 reads gives the same `ReadOutput`, with diagnostics equal apart from their locations, or the same refusal kind, code and location, whatever prefixes it uses for the SACM, XMI and XSI namespaces. This holds for a default namespace, for declarations on the wrapper or on the root, and for a prefix rebound on an inner element. A prefix confers nothing by its spelling: `xmi`, `xsi` or `sacm` bound to another URI is that other namespace, except that a tolerant read reads the `XMI` element and the attributes `id`, `type`, `idref`, `version`, `uuid` and `label` in EMF's `http://www.omg.org/XMI` as XMI 2.5.1's, whatever their prefix; its other names are kept as preserved content (LIB-COMPAT-002 (1)). Namespace URIs compare as exact strings. `xmlns=""` means no namespace, and a refusal says so. Before it is resolved, a type value is collapsed by the XSD white-space rules. An undeclared prefix in a type value, or an unprefixed value with no default namespace, names no SACM class: on a root the type attribute is kept as preserved content with SACM-XMI-003 (D-ROOT-NAME, LIB-COMPAT-003), as in SACM23-XMI-001, and on a child the child is kept whole as preserved content of its parent (SACM23-XMI-016); this departs from C++ `xmi_reader.cpp:597-658` (ADR 0016 D2). | SACM23-XMI-011 | **String values survive XML exactly.** Every string value written as an XML attribute (today an element id and a name's `lang` and `content`) reads back exactly. `xmi::write` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`, and writes TAB, LF and CR as `&#9;`, `&#10;` and `&#13;`, so XML 1.0 §3.3.3 attribute normalisation cannot change them. A string holding a character outside XML 1.0 `Char` makes `xmi::write` fail with `UnrepresentableCharacter` naming the element and the character, and nothing is returned. For a LangString, an absent `lang` or `content` is written as no attribute and reads back absent; an empty one is written as `=""` and reads back empty (ADR 0012). The reader keeps every value exactly, with no trimming or normalisation beyond what XML 1.0 itself does. Every later LangString role inherits these rules. An element whose name is missing is written with no `name` child, and nothing is invented (ADR 0013). `xmi::read` reads one `name` child of every element it reads (a root, SACM23-XMI-001, or a child, SACM23-XMI-016) into that element's name: no `name` child gives no name, and `<name/>` gives a name whose fields are absent. The `name` child may carry only `lang` and `content` in no namespace, an `xmi:id` (SACM23-XMI-022), an `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` naming `LangString` or `ExpressionLangString` and, on an ExpressionLangString, its `expression` (SACM23-BASE-009), and may contain only the value elements `lang` and `content` (SACM23-XMI-014), an ExpressionLangString's one `expression` reference element (SACM23-XMI-015), white space, comments and processing instructions. Anything else on or in it is never dropped and never reinterpreted. Conforming content not read yet (`xmi:uuid` and `xmi:label`, SACM23-XMI-019) is refused as `ReadError::Unsupported` at its location (LIB-API-011). Content that does not conform (any other attribute, including `xml:lang`, which is not SACM `lang`; a type naming a class that is not a LangString, or whose `sacm` prefix is rebound; an element child other than the value elements `lang` and `content`, SACM23-XMI-014, LIB-COMPAT-008) keeps the whole `name` as preserved content of its owner, which then has no name, with one SACM-XMI-003 at the `name` start tag; a `name` element in a namespace is preserved at its start tag (LIB-COMPAT-003, ADR 0033). Non-white-space text, and a single `value` or `content lang`, are LIB-COMPAT-008's C++ shapes (slice 0049). | LIB-COMPAT-001 | **Strict and tolerant load modes.** `ReadOptions` carries a load mode (`xmi::Mode`), strict by default (LIB-API-020), and `ReadOutput::mode()` reports the mode used (ADR 0022). A **strict** read refuses what it cannot read conformantly, as each read row states; a refusal a read row states without naming a mode is a strict read's. A **tolerant** read returns a document for every well-formed input whose roots are SACM packages (ADR 0035 D1, ADR 0041): it refuses only a DOCTYPE, malformed XML, `InvalidRoot`, `NoPackage`, `DuplicateId`, `LimitExceeded` (LIB-SEC-003), and `Unsupported` for an encoding, the parser's capacity, a SACM 2.4 root (LIB-COMPAT-018), an `XMI` element outside XMI 2.5.1 (LIB-COMPAT-002) or an XMI-namespace document element; a root of an older SACM revision or a SACM-like namespace is read as SACM 2.3 with SACM-XMI-008 or SACM-XMI-002 (LIB-COMPAT-004); every other strict refusal is kept as preserved content at its construct (LIB-COMPAT-003), with one Warning at the strict refusal's location: SACM-ENUM-001 for a bad literal (the model holds the default), SACM-MULT-001 for each repeat of a single-valued property (the first occurrence is read), SACM-XMI-005 for an untyped child under an abstract role, SACM-ID-002 for an empty `xmi:id` (the element gets a generated id), and SACM-XMI-007 for a cross-document link not read yet (LIB-API-011). A tolerant read reports no Error. Two read diagnostics are reported, one per attribute, located at its name, neither refusing or changing the document: an `xsi:type` attribute is SACM-XMI-010 (XMI 2.5.1 rule 2g), an Error in strict mode and a Warning in tolerant mode; an `xmi:version` attribute on the `xmi:XMI` element or a root is SACM-XMI-011 (§7.5.3), Info in both modes. LIB-COMPAT-008's C++ shapes read tolerantly with SACM-XMI-012 and are refused strictly as `LegacyShape` (ADR 0022 amendment 1). SACM23-XMI-009's spellings read tolerantly with SACM-XMI-013 and are kept strictly as preserved content with SACM-XMI-013 as an Error.<br>_Note: Slice 0035: designed in ADR 0022 (accepted by the maintainer, 2026-11-13, with SACM-XMI-011 as Info). | SACM23-VAL-001 | **Unique element ids.** `xmi::read`, in both modes, refuses a document in which two or more `xmi:id`s, on elements, on `name`s (SACM23-XMI-022) or inside preserved content (LIB-COMPAT-003), have the same value with `ReadError::DuplicateId`, whose `code()` is SACM-ID-001. It concerns the first id that repeats in document order; `locations()` gives the start tag of every element in the input carrying that id, in document order, and `location()` is the first repeat. | LIB-RT-001 | **Semantic comparison.** `sacm::compare::semantic_compare(left, right) -> Vec<Difference>` compares two documents by their SACM content and lists every difference, naming the element id and the feature; an empty result means equal, and `Document: PartialEq + Eq` means exactly that (ADR 0020). Elements are matched by id. Compared: presence, kind, parent, `gid`, the flags (`isCitation`, `isAbstract`, `isCounter`), every reference end (the derived `expression` through the name and texts that hold it, SACM23-BASE-009), name, the `xmi:id` of the name (`NameId`, SACM23-XMI-022), UtilityElement `content` and TaggedValue `key` with their ids, Artifact `version`, the `date` of an Artifact or an Event, Resource `location` with its ids, Activity `startTime` and `endTime` (SACM23-ART-002, -004 to -007), the `value` of a Term or Expression and a Term's `externalReference` (SACM23-TERM-003, -004), `assertionDeclaration`, preserved content, the order of the roots and the relative order of each element's children across roles. Values are compared exactly: a missing name differs from every present name, including `<name/>` (`LangString::default()`) and `content=""`. Not compared: the generated-id counters, which are not SACM content. Formatting, attribute order and prefixes are not held by a `Document`, except in preserved content, which `==` and `semantic_compare` compare exactly and in order (`Difference::PreservedContent`, reported last for its element; LIB-COMPAT-003). MultiLangString values are compared in order, though the metamodel does not order `value` (UtilityElement `content`, TaggedValue `key` and Resource `location`, SACM23-BASE-004/005, SACM23-ART-005). The result is deterministic and in a fixed order, and comparison never panics.<br>_Note: Slice 0031: designed in ADR 0020. | LIB-CLI-002 | **`sacm validate`.** `sacm validate <file> [--strict \| --tolerant] [--format human\|json]` reads the file strictly by default (`--strict` names the default, `--tolerant` reads in tolerant mode, both together are a usage error), runs `validation::validate` on the document read, and reports the read and validation diagnostics together, sorted (ADR 0023 amendment of 2026-11-16). A file passes only when a strict read accepts it and no diagnostic is an Error. Human format: each diagnostic's `Display` on stdout, then `<file>: <result> (E errors, W warnings, I info)`, where `<result>` is `valid` or `invalid` in strict mode and `readable` or `invalid` with `--tolerant`; tolerant acceptance is never reported as `valid`. A strict refusal of a file that a tolerant read opens prints `<file>: <code\|error> <ReadError>` and `<file>: invalid (refused by a strict read; --tolerant opens it)` on stdout. JSON: one object `{format: 1, file, mode, result, refusal, diagnostics}`, `mode` `strict` or `tolerant`, `result` `valid`, `readable`, `invalid` or `unreadable`; each diagnostic `{code, severity, requirement, clause, location, affected, message}`, keys always present, RFC 8259 escaping; `refusal` is the strict refusal of a file only a tolerant read opens (with `result: "invalid"` and `diagnostics: []`), or the refusal of an unreadable file. Exit 0 when the check passes (`valid`, or `readable` with `--tolerant`), 1 when it fails (an Error diagnostic, or a strict refusal of a file a tolerant read opens), 2 when the arguments are invalid, the file cannot be read from disk, or neither a strict nor a tolerant read opens it; an unreadable file prints `sacm: <file>: <code\|error> <ReadError>`, the refusal in the mode asked for, on stderr in the human format.<br>_Note: Slice 0041: a test input broke §11.4 homogeneity or held two descriptions, which SACM23-VAL-011/012 now report; the input was changed, not the assertion; re-check there. Strict by default: the maintainer, 2026-11-16 (slice 0054), after the review found a tolerant read could report a non-conforming file as valid. Slice 0063: refusals carry codes, templates and arguments (LIB-API-017); re-check there. | LIB-CLI-003 | **`sacm roundtrip`.** `sacm roundtrip <file> [--strict] [-o <out>]` reads the file (tolerant by default), writes it in strict mode to memory, reads that output back in strict mode, and compares the two with `compare::semantic_compare` (ADR 0023). It prints each `Difference` on one line, then `<file>: round trip ok` or `<file>: round trip failed: <reason>`. Exit 0 when the strict save succeeds, the output reads back with no Error and there is no difference; 1 when the strict save refuses (each Error printed), the output does not read back cleanly, or there is a difference; 2 when the input cannot be read, `-o` cannot be written, or the arguments are invalid. `-o <out>` writes the strict output only when the round trip is faithful.<br>_Note: Slice 0038 (M1 audit): `--strict` was documented but untested; a test is added; re-check required. | SACM23-XMI-014 | **Element form of single-valued values.** `xmi::read` reads, in both modes and with no diagnostic, the XML element form of the single-valued DataType properties it reads today: a `name`'s `lang` and `content`, and an Assertion's `assertionDeclaration` (a Claim and the five asserted relationship kinds, SACM23-ARG-007); `gid` (SACM23-BASE-006), `isCitation` and `isAbstract` (SACM23-BASE-007/008), `isCounter` (SACM23-ARG-007), `version`, `date`, `startTime` and `endTime` (SACM23-ART-002, -004, -006, -007), an ExpressionElement's `value` and a Term's `externalReference` (SACM23-TERM-003, -004) and a `value`'s `lang` and `content` (SACM23-BASE-004) use it too. A value element is in no namespace, carries no attribute and has no element children; its value is its character content exactly (CDATA and references give their characters, comments and processing instructions are ignored, nothing is trimmed: XSD `preserve`), an empty element is the empty string, and an `assertionDeclaration` value must be one of the six literals exactly. The element may appear anywhere among its siblings, and the attribute and element forms may be mixed across different properties. The same document in either form reads to an equal `Document`, and export writes the attribute form. A property written both as an attribute and as an element, or as two elements, is refused in strict mode as `ReadError::RepeatedValue` (SACM-MULT-001), naming every occurrence, even when the values are equal (the maintainer, 2026-11-13); a tolerant read keeps the first occurrence and preserves each later one, with a SACM-MULT-001 Warning (LIB-COMPAT-001). A value element with an attribute (`xmi:id`, a type or another), an element child, or a namespace other than XMI does not conform: the `name` holding it, or the value element itself when it sits directly on its owner (`assertionDeclaration`, `gid`, a flag, `version`, `date`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `value`, `externalReference`), is kept whole as preserved content of the owner, with one SACM-XMI-003 at its start tag (LIB-COMPAT-003, ADR 0033); one in the XMI namespace is kept as preserved content with SACM-XMI-003, except `xmi:extension` and `xmi:Extension`, which are XMI metadata (SACM23-XMI-019); `xsi:nil` is read (SACM23-XMI-026) and the legacy `lang` on a `content` in a `name` is a LIB-COMPAT-008 shape (slice 0049); inside a `value` it keeps the whole `name`, `content`, `key` or `location` as preserved content; a bad literal is `ReadError::InvalidLiteral` at the start tag (SACM23-VAL-006).<br>_Note: Slice 0039: reworded for SACM23-XMI-020/-021/-022/-025 and SACM23-VAL-006 (ADR 0024, ADR 0021 amendment 2); re-check there. | LIB-API-008 | **Containment legality.** The model knows, for every (parent kind, child kind) pair, whether a SACM 2.3 composite role of the parent's class admits the child, per ptc/22-03-13 with the inventory's recorded divergences. Subclasses inherit roles, package interfaces and bindings included. Every insertion refuses a child whose kind no role of the parent's class admits, and leaves the document unchanged; this binds the crate-internal insertion that the XMI reader and the create operations use, and the test-support `insert`; `MoveElement` and `CopyElements` check the same table before they change anything (LIB-EDIT-017, LIB-EDIT-018). ArtifactPackage `artifactElement` admits every ArtifactElement kind, as the metamodel types it (ADR 0014). A root must be a package kind (`ElementKind::is_package`: the four packages, their interfaces and bindings; ADR 0010 D1 "of any package kind"); any other root is refused with `InsertError::RootNotAllowed`, as C++ refuses it (`io/xmi_reader.cpp` read_root, `is_package_kind`, `kXmiInvalidRoot`). Multiplicity is not enforced on insertion (D-VAL-LAYER, D-DESC-MULT). | SACM23-XMI-016 | **Containment children conform to their role.** `xmi::read` reads each containment child under its role element: an element in no namespace whose local name is a composite role of the parent's class, as spelled in ptc/22-03-13. The child's class is the one its `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` names, resolved as for roots (SACM23-XMI-002); without a type attribute it is the role's declared type, if that type is concrete (XMI 2.5.1 §7.6.3). The child is read with its `xmi:id`, its name (SACM23-XMI-012) and its parent, in document order across roles (ADR 0010 D2). Every child kind a role of the parent's class admits is read in that role (LIB-API-008); each may carry only namespace declarations, `xmi:id`, a type attribute, one `name`, one `gid` (SACM23-BASE-006), utility children (SACM23-BASE-004/005) the flags, references and string attributes (`version`, `date`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `value`, `externalReference`; SACM23-ART-002, -004, -006, -007, SACM23-TERM-003, -004) its class has (ADR 0026, ADR 0027), a Resource's one `location` (SACM23-ART-005) and, on an Assertion, one `assertionDeclaration` as an attribute or an element (SACM23-XMI-017, SACM23-XMI-014). A child is never re-roled, re-typed or dropped. A child whose type does not conform to its role, names an abstract or unknown class, or disagrees with its other type attribute, a child under a role the parent's class lacks or in a namespace other than XMI, and any other element are kept whole as preserved content of the parent, at the child's start tag; an attribute the child's class lacks (`xmi:version` included) and non-white-space text are kept as preserved content of the child, at the attribute's name or the text; each gives one SACM-XMI-003 (LIB-COMPAT-003, ADR 0033). Conforming content not read yet is refused as `ReadError::Unsupported` at the child's start tag, or at an attribute's name (LIB-API-011): XMI-namespace content such as `xmi:Extension`, `xmi:uuid` or `xmi:label` (SACM23-XMI-019). The spellings `argumentationElement` and `sacm:ArtifactAssertedRelationship` follow SACM23-XMI-009, and `TerminologyElement` SACM23-XMI-028. | SACM23-XMI-018 | **UTF-16 input.** `xmi::read` reads UTF-16 input that begins with a byte order mark (`FF FE` little-endian, `FE FF` big-endian, not followed by `00 00`). It decodes the input with std only (`u16::from_le_bytes`/`from_be_bytes`, `char::decode_utf16`) and then reads it exactly as the same characters in UTF-8, so the `ReadOutput` or `ReadError` is the same. Locations count characters as for UTF-8, and the byte order mark takes no column. The encoding declaration may be absent or name `UTF-16`, `UTF-16LE` or `UTF-16BE`, in any letter case. Any other declared name contradicts the mark and is `Malformed` (SACM-XML-001, XML 1.0 §4.3.3). So are an odd byte count and an unpaired surrogate. Everything else stays `Unsupported`, as in LIB-API-009: UTF-16 without a byte order mark (nothing is guessed), UTF-32 and UCS-4, and a UTF-16 name declared in UTF-8 input. This is the minimal UTF-16 support the maintainer chose on 2026-11-12 (ADR 0005 B2 amendment 1).<br>_Note: Slice 0036: tests updated for the coded id refusals (ADR 0015 amendment 2); re-checked there. A test reads the suite's 21 catalogs and runs through `xmi::read` every TEST with TYPE `not-wf`, RECOMMENDATION XML1.0 (the default), XML1.0-errata2e/3e/4e, NS1.0 or NS1.0-errata1e, VERSION absent or listing 1.0, and EDITION absent or listing 5. Each is refused: `Malformed` or `Doctype`, or `Unsupported` only from the encoding steps; a root-stage result (`Ok`, `InvalidRoot`, `NoPackage`, root-stage `Unsupported`) counts as accepted, because the suite's documents are not SACM. The one case roxmltree 0.21.2 accepts, rmt-ns10-032 (`xmlns:xmlns` declared), is refused by a new check (Namespaces 1.0 §3), so the list of accepted cases is empty and the parser's leniencies within the suite form a closed, reviewed list. Valid and invalid XML 1.0 and NS 1.0 cases that reach the root stage are never refused as `Malformed` (a guard against an over-strict scan). | SACM23-VAL-006 | **Enumeration literals.** A strict `xmi::read` refuses an `assertionDeclaration` value that is not exactly one of the six AssertionDeclaration literals, in the attribute form (SACM23-XMI-017) or the element form (SACM23-XMI-014), as `ReadError::InvalidLiteral { element, property, value, location }` whose `code()` is SACM-ENUM-001 (ADR 0021 amendment 2). `value` is the value as read: after XML attribute-value normalisation for the attribute, the exact character content for the element. | SACM23-BASE-004 | **Descriptions, notes and implementation constraints.** Every ModelElement holds its `description`, `implementationConstraint` and `note` children (UtilityElements, §8.7-§8.9, §8.11) as elements with an id and a kind, in document order across roles (D-ORDER), accessed through `SacmElement::descriptions()`, `implementation_constraints()` and `notes()`; several descriptions are kept (D-DESC-MULT) (ADR 0025). A UtilityElement's `content()` is `None` (no `content` child) or a MultiLangString (`<content/>` is empty), and both round-trip. A MultiLangString is written as its role element with one `value` child per LangString, in order and with duplicates; each `value` follows the `name` LangString rules (SACM23-XMI-012, -014). Several `value` children are kept; a second `content` is `RepeatedValue` (SACM23-XMI-021). An `xmi:id` on a `content` element or a `value` is kept by role and position (`content_id()`, `content_value_ids()`), shares the file's id space, is written back and compared (ADR 0024). A UtilityElement has no `name`. A role element with `lang`/`content` attributes or text and no `value` children, and `content=` or text on a UtilityElement, are the C++ shapes of LIB-COMPAT-008: read with a SACM-XMI-012 Warning in tolerant mode, refused as `LegacyShape` in strict mode. They are created by `CreateDescription`, `CreateImplementationConstraint` and `CreateNote` under the LIB-EDIT-001 contract; changing content is LIB-EDIT-008 and removal LIB-EDIT-004/005. | SACM23-XMI-005 | **Reference serialization.** A non-containment reference is read from, and written as, an XML attribute in no namespace named by the reference end, whose value is the targets' ids separated by XML white space (xsd:IDREFS; XMI 2.5.1 rules 2h, 2j, 4i) (ADR 0026). In this release the ends are `citedElement` and `abstractForm` (SACM23-BASE-007/008), `metaClaim` (SACM23-ARG-004), `structure` (SACM23-ARG-005), `referencedArtifactElement` (SACM23-ARG-006), `source`, `target` and `reasoning` (SACM23-ARG-007), an ArgumentGroup's `argumentElement` (SACM23-ARG-013), an ArtifactGroup's `artifactElement` (SACM23-ART-011) and an ArtifactAssetRelationship's `source` and `target` (SACM23-ART-010), a package's `interface`, an interface's `implements` and a binding's `participantPackage` (SACM23-ARG-014, SACM23-ARG-015, SACM23-ART-012, SACM23-ART-013, SACM23-AC-002, SACM23-AC-003, SACM23-TERM-007, SACM23-TERM-008); each later end's row inherits the rule. A reference is held as the target id, each token exactly as read (no `#` stripped), and resolves by id across the whole input whatever the order (a later element, another root, the element itself). A reference naming no element (an id absent from the file, or a `name`, `content`, `key`, `location` or `value` id) is kept, written back and reported by `validate` (SACM23-VAL-003); it is never dropped. Two or more ids on a single-valued end is `RepeatedValue` (SACM-MULT-001); an empty or all-white-space value, and `sacm:citedElement`, are kept as preserved content of the element, with SACM-XMI-003 at the attribute's name, never read as absent (LIB-COMPAT-003). Generated ids, in the reader and in edits, skip every referenced id. `xmi::write` writes the ids separated by one space, after the SACMElement flags.<br>_Note: Slice 0057: reworded for ArtifactAssetRelationship and the SACM23-XMI-009 spellings; re-check there. | SACM23-ARG-004 | **metaClaim.** Every element of an Assertion kind (Claim and the five asserted relationship kinds) holds `metaClaim`, a multi-valued reference end typed Claim (§11.10 `[0..*]`), as ids in document order with repeats (`SacmElement::meta_claims() -> &[ElementId]`, empty by default; ADR 0026, ADR 0027). It is the first multi-valued end (`ReferenceEnd::is_many()`): the attribute keeps every token in order, and each `<metaClaim>` element appends one id; an attribute and elements for the end is `RepeatedValue`. It is written as one attribute, ids separated by one space, after `assertionDeclaration`, and compared in order (`Difference::MetaClaims`). A dangling id is SACM-REF-001 with clause `11.10`; a non-Claim target is held (SACM23-VAL-004). | SACM23-XMI-015 | **Element form of references.** Both load modes read a reference given as an empty element in no namespace named by the end, with exactly one link attribute: `xmi:idref="id"` (rule 2l) or an unqualified `href="#id"` (rule 2n, the same document); the value is trimmed (xsd:IDREF, anyURI) and the element may hold only white space, comments and processing instructions (ADR 0026). It reads to a model equal to the attribute form, and `write` writes the attribute form, unless the end also holds a cross-document `href` (SACM23-XMI-027) or a preserved attribute of its name (ADR 0033), which it writes in element form. An attribute and an element for the same end, or two elements on a single-valued end, is `RepeatedValue` (rule 2h). A reference element that does not conform (both link attributes or neither, an empty or all-white-space `xmi:idref` included; an `xmi:idref` with white space inside it; another attribute, such as an unqualified `idref` or `xmi:href`; a child element or text; a namespace-qualified reference element) is kept whole as preserved content of its owner, with one SACM-XMI-003 at its start tag and the end absent (LIB-COMPAT-003, ADR 0033). A type attribute or an identity attribute (`xmi:id`, `xmi:uuid`, `xmi:label`) on it keeps it whole with SACM-XMI-003 (production 2c, rule 4e; ADR 0042); `Unsupported` at the attribute: an `href` whose fragment holds `(` or `)` (SACM23-XMI-029). An `href` with a document part is read as a cross-document reference (SACM23-XMI-027). One with no `#`, an empty fragment, a `#` in its fragment or XML white space inside it keeps the whole element as preserved content with SACM-XMI-003.<br>_Note: Slice 0068: cross-document references (SACM23-XMI-027) count as values of their end and are never SACM-REF findings; the modularity rules (SACM23-VAL-013 to -015, -023) are live; re-check there. | LIB-COMPAT-003 | **Unknown content is preserved, not dropped.** `xmi::read` keeps, in both modes, every attribute, child element (with its subtree) and non-white-space text that the SACM XML Schema and the XMI 2.5.1 production rules do not allow where it stands and that no row reads as a tolerance, as preserved content of the element it sits in (ADR 0033). Each gives one SACM-XMI-003 (`Code::XMI_UNKNOWN_CONTENT`; Warning tolerant, Error strict) at it, affecting that element. Nothing inside a preserved subtree is read or reported, but its `xmi:id`s are checked (an empty one is SACM-ID-002 in tolerant mode). Preserved content keeps its position (a child at its index among the element's children; attributes after the typed ones, in input order) and its namespace URIs, local names, prefixes and values exactly, except that a kept type attribute's value may have its prefix renamed, and an element keeping only an EMF `type` or an `xsi:type` gains its own `xmi:type`, on write (LIB-COMPAT-019). A tolerant `xmi::write` writes it back, so load → save → load gives an equal `Document` and a re-write is byte-identical, except, in both, for a root attribute in another XMI namespace, such as XMI 2.4.1's `http://www.omg.org/spec/XMI/20110701`, which is renamed on write and leaves an extra binding on each holder of preserved content (EMF's `http://www.omg.org/XMI` is read since slice 0075a, LIB-COMPAT-002); a strict write refuses it (SACM23-XMI-008). `==` and `semantic_compare` compare it exactly and in order (`Difference::PreservedContent`). Its ids stay in the document's id space; a typed reference to one is SACM-REF-003. Deleting a holder removes its preserved content. Since slices 0073a and 0073b every conforming construct is read, so no input gives SACM-XMI-014 (SACM23-XMI-019, SACM23-XMI-029). A document also holds preserved content outside its elements: wrapper attributes other than XMI metadata, XMI-namespace wrapper children that XMI 2.5.1 does not define there, and text, placed among the roots, moved by root creates, deletes and reorders, and exposed by `Document::has_preserved_content` and `Difference::DocumentPreservedContent` (ADR 0035 D3). A preserved attribute whose prefix binds `sacm` or `xmi` to another URI is a strict refusal; a tolerant read keeps it, with its prefix replaced by the first `nsN` unbound at the holder. Known gap: a prefix used only inside a preserved attribute's value (a QName such as `v:ref="u:thing"`) is not declared on write, so its binding is lost on a tolerant save (LIB-COMPAT-013).<br>_Note: Maintainer decisions 2026-11-14 (strict keeps with an Error) and 2026-11-15 (only non-conforming content; a preserved child element counts for RejectIfNonEmpty; a root type naming another class is preserved; a discard edit is LIB-EDIT-016, M6). The design and worked example are in ADR 0033 and the slice 0050 brief. Slice 0062: reworded for the Terminology kinds; re-check there. Slice 0067: every SACM 2.3 kind and end is read; the unread-kind refusals and their templates are removed (SACM23-TERM-007, -008, SACM23-AC-002, -003); re-check there. Slice 0072: four corpus files (8, 9, 12, 13) now open tolerantly and show the XMI-namespace exception; nothing is lost (LIB-COMPAT-002). Slice 0073a: XMI metadata (SACM23-XMI-019, ADR 0042) and same-file proxies (SACM23-XMI-030) are read; re-check there. Slices 0075a, 0075b and 0076: the EMF alias, declared subclasses and kept-type writes change what is preserved and how it is written; tests pass; re-checked at the M6 close (slice 0080)._ | xmi | ADR | LIB-EDIT-009 | **Reference edits.** Operations cover every reference end: `citedElement`, `abstractForm` (§8.2), `metaClaim` (§11.10), `reasoning`, `source`, `target` (§11.13), `structure` (§11.12), `referencedArtifactElement` (§11.9), an ArgumentGroup's `argumentElement` (§11.2), an ArtifactGroup's `artifactElement` (§12.3) and an ArtifactAssetRelationship's `source` and `target` (§12.14), a package's `interface` (§9.2; ptc/22-03-13), an interface's `implements` (§9.3, §10.5, §11.6, §12.5) and a binding's `participantPackage` (§9.4, §10.6, §11.5, §12.4). They refuse the derived `expression` (`ReferenceEnd::Expression`, SACM23-BASE-009) as `EditError::DerivedEnd` (SACM-CMD-008), after an unknown element. `SetReferences` replaces an end's ids in order with repeats kept (`clear` empties it), `AddReference` appends one, and `RemoveReference` drops every occurrence of one, each within the end's multiplicity (`target` cannot be emptied; `implements` holds exactly one id and `participantPackage` at least two distinct values, ids and cross-document `href`s counted, ADR 0040 D5; `SetReferences` and `clear` also remove the end's `href`s, which `AddReference` and `RemoveReference` keep). They refuse, in order: an unknown element (`ElementNotFound`, SACM-CMD-001), a kind without the end (SACM-CMD-008), for a remove an id the end does not hold (`ReferenceNotHeld`, SACM-CMD-001), fewer distinct values than the lower bound (`TooFewReferences`) or more than one on a single-valued end (`TooManyReferences`, both SACM-MULT-001), an id holding white space (`InvalidReference`), an id naming no element (`ReferenceNotFound`) and a wrongly typed id (`WrongReferenceType`); the last three check only ids the end does not already hold (C++'s repair exception, per end). Content rules are never refused: §11.15/§11.17/§11.18, SACM-CITE-001, SACM-ABS-001, repeats (SACM23-VAL-022) and self-references. `changed_ids` is `[owner]` exactly when the end changes, or when an edit that leaves the end non-empty replaces a preserved attribute of the end's name on the owner (such as `metaClaim=""`), which it removes; clearing the end keeps it (ADR 0033).<br>_Note: Slice 0042: when an edit can replace a reference, kill the `IdUse::is_unused -> false` mutant excluded for this row in docs/quality/mutants-triage.md, and remove its exclusion. Lead decisions: a replaced name or content keeps its role element's `xmi:id` and its value ids by position (D-PRESERVE); removing an id removes every occurrence, and an id the end does not hold is refused. | LIB-EDIT-010 | **Reorder contained elements.** `ReorderElements` reorders the direct children of any element (`new(parent, order)`) or the document's roots (`roots(order)`): it names a subset in a new order and writes them back into the positions they occupy, every other child keeping its position; roles, parents, ids and counters do not change. It refuses, in order: an unknown parent (SACM-CMD-001), an empty list (SACM-CMD-009), then, id by id in list order, an id that is not a direct child or root (`ChildNotFound`, SACM-CMD-001) and an id named before (SACM-CMD-009). Lead decisions: a replaced name or content keeps its role element's `xmi:id` and its value ids by position (D-PRESERVE); removing an id removes every occurrence, and an id the end does not hold is refused. | LIB-QA-018 | **Documentation-only pushes skip the code-only CI jobs.** A CI job `changes` decides whether the latest push (a pull request's new commits, or a push's before..after) changed any file outside `docs/`, and is true when it cannot tell. A push compared with the commit before it (a pull request's `synchronize`, or a push) is docs-only only if CI succeeded on that commit, so a docs-only push never turns failed, cancelled or unfinished code checks green (Copilot review on #67); a newly opened pull request compares with its base. Only an explicit `false` skips anything: the Windows and macOS test steps, the MSRV job and the PR-diff mutant shards; their required checks pass as skipped. The Ubuntu tests and every other job still run. | LIB-API-006 | **serde support for edit and diagnostic values.** An optional `serde` feature implements `Serialize` and `Deserialize` for `Operation` and every operation struct, `Mutation`, `EditError`, the value types they carry (`ElementId`, `ElementKind`, `LangString`, `MultiLangString`, `AssertionDeclaration` and the edit selectors), for `Diagnostic`, `Code`, `Severity` and `SourceLocation`, and for `ReadError`, `WriteError` and `WriteAttribute` (LIB-API-017). The one exception is `CopyElements`, which holds a snapshot of another document: serializing an `Operation::CopyElements`, or a value that holds one, is an error, and its tag does not deserialize (ADR 0030 amendment 2). `Document` does not implement them: XMI stays the only serialization of the model. A deserialized operation is checked by `edit::apply` exactly as a constructed one, and an unknown `Code` or kind name is a deserialization error. The serialized form is documented and golden-tested in JSON; the goldens guard against accidental change, and the shape changes only in a semver-breaking release (ADR 0030 amendment 1; the maintainer, 2026-11-16).<br>_Note: Narrowed 2026-11-15 from "serializes the model and diagnostics": leaving `Document` out removes the concern that serde freezes a second serialization of the model. The maintainer decided on 2026-11-15 that the serialized form is a stability promise, like `operation_name()`: changing it is a breaking change. Needs an ADR for the serde dependency (optional, with `derive`) and the JSON shape. LIB-QA-017 builds the wasm target with this feature too. ## M3 — Artifact model and a first release

The Artifact package (packages, assets, properties, relationships and groups, with their date-typed attributes and model-spelling variants), and what an application needs before M4 and M5: real files read, move and copy edits, `referrers`, an undo decision, `has_errors` and a first crates.io release (the maintainer, 2026-11-16).

| SACM23-ART-001 | **ArtifactPackage.** ArtifactPackage (§12.2) is read and written as a root (bare or inside `xmi:XMI`), in an AssuranceCasePackage's `artifactPackage` role, and nested in another ArtifactPackage's `artifactElement` role with `xmi:type`; it holds its ArtifactElements in the composite role `artifactElement : ArtifactElement [0..*]` in document order (every ArtifactElement kind is admitted: LIB-API-008, ADR 0014), so the kinds already readable are also read inside it. An untyped `artifactElement` child is `MissingType` (SACM-XMI-005); one in reference form is a proxy: of a root of the same document, moved into place (SACM23-XMI-030), or of an element of another document, a cross-document link not read yet (SACM23-XMI-029). Every ArtifactElement kind is read in `artifactElement`, the interface and binding kinds included, and so is its `interface` end (SACM23-ART-012); the type `ArtifactAssertedRelationship` is a spelling read as SACM23-XMI-009 says. `edit::CreateArtifactPackage` creates one as a root or a child (ADR 0034).<br>_Note: Slice 0055: reworded because Artifact, Resource, Activity and Event are read now (ADR 0034 amendment 1); re-check there. | SACM23-ART-002 | **Date-typed attributes.** The four attributes formal/23-05-08 types `date`, Artifact `date` (§12.7), Event `date` (§12.9) and Activity `startTime` and `endTime` (§12.11), are each held as an optional string exactly as written: `SacmElement::date()` (Artifact and Event), `start_time()` and `end_time()` (D-DATE). SACM 2.3 defines no lexical form for `date`, ptc/22-03-13 types them by a link into a MagicDraw library (spec defect D17), and the SACM XML Schema the XMI rules produce types them `xsd:string`, so every value, `""` included, is read in both modes with no diagnostic and written back exactly; nothing parses, trims or normalises it. Each is read from its XML attribute or its value element (SACM23-XMI-014), `xsi:nil` included (SACM23-XMI-026); given twice it is `RepeatedValue` (SACM-MULT-001; tolerant: LIB-COMPAT-001), and on a kind that lacks it, it is preserved content (SACM-XMI-003). | SACM23-ART-005 | **Resource.** Resource (§12.10, superclass ArtifactAsset) is read and written typed in an ArtifactPackage's `artifactElement`, with its Base features, its `property` children and its `location` (text followed: D-TEXT-MODEL, spec defect D5). `location` is a MultiLangString role, read and written by SACM23-BASE-004's rules for a UtilityElement's `content`: absent kept apart from empty, values in order with duplicates, an `xmi:id` on `location` and on each `value` kept by position (`SacmElement::location()`, `location_id()`, `location_value_ids()`), a second `location` `RepeatedValue`. It is written directly after `name`. | SACM23-ART-010 | **ArtifactAssetRelationship.** ArtifactAssetRelationship (§12.14; its name and superclass ArtifactAsset follow the text, D-TEXT-MODEL) is read and written typed in an ArtifactPackage's `artifactElement`, with its Base features, its `property` children (SACM23-ART-003) and the reference ends `source : ArtifactAsset [1..*]` and `target : ArtifactAsset [1..*]`, held as `ReferenceEnd::ArtifactSource` and `ReferenceEnd::ArtifactTarget`: XMI names `source` and `target`, serde names `artifactSource` and `artifactTarget`, because `Source` and `Target` are an AssertedRelationship's ends (the maintainer's M3 decision 5). `SacmElement::sources()` and the new `targets()` answer for it and for every AssertedRelationship; `target()` stays the AssertedRelationship's. Each end follows SACM23-XMI-005/015 (serialization), SACM23-VAL-003/004/022 (dangling, typing to ArtifactAsset, repeats; clause `12.14`) and LIB-EDIT-009 (edits; each end keeps at least one id). `validation::validate` reports a relationship with no `source`, and one with no `target`, as one SACM-MULT-001 Error per missing end, because the text and the model agree on `[1..*]` (D-SEV). `edit::CreateArtifactAssetRelationship::new(parent, name, sources, targets)` creates one. Under LIB-EDIT-005, `DeleteReferencingRelationships` deletes a relationship whose `source` or `target` names a deleted element, and `ScrubReferences` deletes one left with no `source` or no `target` (decision 7). `semantic_compare` reports `Difference::ArtifactSources` and `Difference::ArtifactTargets`.<br>_Note: Slice 0062: reworded for the Terminology kinds; re-check there. | LIB-EDIT-011 | **Undo: the decided approach.** Undo and redo are the application's: the `edit` module docs show a history of whole documents, a `Document::clone` taken before each successful `edit::apply`, `edit::apply_preview`, `edit::batch` or `edit::apply_all` and restored with `std::mem::replace`, so one operation, one batch or an accepted draft (`CopyElements` in a batch) is one step. A restored clone is `==` to the document before the change and writes the same XMI, preserved content included; it has the revision and the generated-id counters it had, so the next create generates the id an undone create had (D-ID; an application that needs ids unique across its history gives its own, ADR 0031), and a preview taken before an undone change applies again after the undo. The docs say a step costs one clone, in time and memory proportional to the document, and leave the depth to the application. The crate has no history type and no inverse operations (ADR 0037, D-UNDO).<br>_Note: Requirements from Assurance Forge (GitHub issue #61, 2026-11-14), input to Q-UNDO: one user action, even a batch (LIB-EDIT-014), is one undo step; accepting a draft `Document` into the main one is one step; the generated ids after an undo are specified (reused or not); history is per document and in memory; memory use is bounded for cases of thousands of elements. The web client sends changes as operations, which favours inverse operations over snapshots. Measured 2026-11-15 (release build, flat package of claims): `Document::clone` 0.26 ms at 1,000 elements, 1.4 ms at 5,000, 7.8 ms at 20,000; `==` and `semantic_compare` 0.8 ms at 5,000 but 12-16 ms at 20,000 (super-linear)._ | editing | Q-UNDO and D-RESULT; D-UNDO; GitHub issue #61; ADR 0037 (accepted by the maintainer, 2026-11-17) | `verified` | LIB-EDIT-005, LIB-EDIT-009, LIB-EDIT-014, LIB-EDIT-018 | `lib_edit_011_undoing_a_batch_restores_an_equal_document_that_writes_the_same_xmi_and_generates_the_same_next_id`<br>`lib_edit_011_undoing_a_delete_restores_preserved_content_and_file_ids`<br>`lib_edit_011_accepting_a_draft_is_one_step`<br>`lib_edit_011_undo_and_redo_restore_the_revision`<br>`lib_edit_011_a_preview_taken_before_an_undone_change_applies_after_the_undo`<br>`lib_edit_011_a_refused_change_records_no_step` |
| LIB-COMPAT-015 | **Real files are read.** `cargo xtask fetch-corpus` downloads SACM files that tools other than this crate wrote, at URLs pinned to a commit with SHA-256 pins (`CORPUS` in `xtask/src/fetch.rs`), into the git-ignored `third_party/corpus/`, with the policy of `fetch-spec`; they are never committed. An xtask test reads each file tolerantly and strictly, validates the document a tolerant read returns, writes it back tolerantly and reads that back, and reports per file the outcome of each step, the diagnostics by code and severity with counts, and whether the write-back reads back semantically equal. | LIB-EDIT-017 | **Move an element.** A `MoveElement` operation moves an element, with everything it contains and its preserved content, under another parent (`new`) or to the roots (`root`), after the last child or root, or at a position (`with_position`): its index among the new parent's children (or the roots) after the move, from 0 to the number of the others. Ids, references and the element's features do not change; its parent, its role and the order do. The containment table decides the legal parents (`InvalidParent`), and a root must be a package (`InvalidRoot`). Moving an element into itself or an element it contains is `ParentInSubtree`, and a position past the end is `PositionOutOfRange`. Moving under a parent an element that keeps `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` as preserved content, which only a root can carry, is `KeptRootType` (SACM-CMD-005, LIB-COMPAT-019), checked after `ParentInSubtree` and before `PositionOutOfRange`. A preserved child of either parent keeps its place after the typed child it followed. `changed_ids` follow LIB-EDIT-003: the element when its parent changes, and a parent whose child order or preserved placement changes, in pre-order after. A move to the place the element holds changes nothing. | LIB-EDIT-018 | **Copy elements from another document.** `CopyElements` copies elements of a source `Document`, each with everything it contains, under a parent of the target (`new`) or as roots (`root`), after the last child or root, in the order given, so an application can accept a draft built in another document (GitHub issue #61). The source elements are captured when the operation is built (`ElementNotFound` for an id the source lacks); an element listed twice, or inside another listed element, is copied once. An element keeps its id when it is an NCName free in the target (no element, part or preserved content holds it and no reference names it); otherwise it gets a generated id that avoids every id the copy keeps or names. A name, `content`, `key`, `location` or `value` keeps its `xmi:id` when it is an NCName free in the target, and is copied without one otherwise. A reference to a copied element follows its new id; every other reference is kept as written. The copy is checked as a create: the parent (`ParentNotFound`, `InvalidParent`, `InvalidRoot`, and `KeptRootType` for a listed element that keeps `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` copied under a parent, after its `InvalidParent`, LIB-COMPAT-019), the preserved content's ids (`DuplicateId`), required ends (`TooFewReferences`), and every reference against the target and the copies (`ReferenceNotFound`, `WrongReferenceType`; a typed end never holds an id with white space, so `InvalidReference` cannot arise). An unknown parent is `ParentNotFound` even for an empty list. Everything else, preserved content included, is copied exactly. The `Mutation` lists the created ids in pre-order, the i-th being the copy of `source_ids()[i]`, and changes and deletes nothing. It works with `check`, `preview` and batches. It is the one operation serde does not serialize (ADR 0030 amendment 2).<br>_Note: Slice 0068: cross-document references (SACM23-XMI-027) count as values of their end and are never SACM-REF findings; the modularity rules (SACM23-VAL-013 to -015, -023) are live; re-check there. | LIB-API-014 | **Who references an element.** `Document::referrers(id)` lists every typed reference that names `id`, whether or not an element has that id: the holder, the end and the id's position in the end. They are ordered by holder in document pre-order, then by end in `ReferenceEnd::ALL` order, then by position; an id held twice in one end gives two entries. References preserved content may hold are not typed and are not listed. So an application can answer "what supports this claim?" without walking every element. | LIB-API-015 | **Public flag and reference-end readers.** `SacmElement::flag(Flag)` and `SacmElement::references(ReferenceEnd)` are public: a flag the kind lacks is `false`, and an end it lacks holds no id. `Flag::ALL` and `ReferenceEnd::ALL` list every flag and end in a documented order, as `&'static` slices so a later variant is additive. `Flag::applies_to(kind)` and `ReferenceEnd::applies_to(kind)` say whether an element of `kind` has it. `ReferenceEnd::bounds(kind)` gives the fewest and most ids the end holds on an element of `kind`, as `(lower, upper)` with `None` for no upper bound, and `None` when the kind has no such end; bounds depend on the owner (§11.13 `target:ArgumentAsset[1]`; §12.14 `target:ArtifactAsset[1..*]` for an ArtifactAssetRelationship, `ReferenceEnd::ArtifactTarget`). So a generic property panel can list an element's flags and ends without mapping each variant by hand. | SACM23-BASE-009 | **ExpressionLangString.** ExpressionLangString (§8.4, a LangString) is a form of `LangString`: plain, or an ExpressionLangString with an optional `expression` id (ADR 0038). `LangString::expression()`, `is_expression_lang_string()`, `with_expression(id)` and `without_expression()` read and set it, and `Eq`, `Ord` and `Hash` tell the forms apart. Every LangString place can hold one: a name (§8.6) and each value of a `content` (§8.7), `key` (§8.12) or `location` (§12.10). Both load modes read a `name` or `value` typed `sacm:ExpressionLangString` (`xmi:type`, or `xsi:type` with SACM-XMI-010). Its `expression` is read as an IDREF attribute or as one reference element, under the SACM23-XMI-005 and SACM23-XMI-015 rules; two ids, or an attribute and an element, is `RepeatedValue` of `<property>.expression`. `xmi::write` writes `xmi:type="sacm:ExpressionLangString"`, then the `xmi:id`, `lang` and `content`, then `expression="id"`. These do not conform and keep the whole name or text as preserved content with SACM-XMI-003: an `expression` attribute or element on an untyped or LangString-typed `name` or `value`; an empty `expression`; a reference element that does not conform; and an ExpressionLangString `value` inside a `name`, and a `value` inside a `name` typed ExpressionLangString. `ReferenceEnd::Expression` (`expression`, clause 8.4, `[0..*]`, type ExpressionElement, on every kind) is derived. It holds the element's expression ids in write order: the name, then the values of `content`, `key` and `location`. `SacmElement::expressions()` reads it, and `Document::referrers` and delete previews list it. SACM23-VAL-003 and SACM23-VAL-004 check it with clause `8.4`, and so does the strict-save schema check; SACM23-VAL-022 does not. It is compared through the name and the texts. `SetReferences`, `AddReference` and `RemoveReference` refuse it as `EditError::DerivedEnd` (SACM-CMD-008). Every create, `SetName`, `SetContent`, `SetKey`, `SetLocation` and `CopyElements` check the expression ids they add as reference ids (`InvalidReference`, `ReferenceNotFound`, `WrongReferenceType`, end `expression`). They refuse an ExpressionLangString with no expression as `TooFewReferences`. On delete, `RejectIfReferenced` refuses an expression that names a deleted element. `ScrubReferences` and `DeleteReferencingRelationships` make each such ExpressionLangString plain, keeping `lang` and `content`, and put the holder in `changed_ids`. `validate` reports an ExpressionLangString with no expression as one SACM-MULT-001 Error (clause 8.4; spec defect D20). With `serde` an ExpressionLangString is `{"type":"ExpressionLangString","lang","content","expression"}` (ADR 0030 amendment 4).<br>_Note: Slice 0067: every SACM 2.3 kind and end is read; the unread-kind refusals and their templates are removed (SACM23-TERM-007, -008, SACM23-AC-002, -003); re-check there. | LIB-API-017 | **Every read and write refusal has a code, a template and arguments.** Every `ReadError` and `WriteError` has a catalog code, a message template and the template's arguments. `ReadError::code()` and `WriteError::code()` return a `Code`, not an `Option` (Breaking, 0.2.0). `ReadError::Unsupported` takes the code that a tolerant read gives the same input, by refusal-list entry: a `Defect`: SACM-XMI-003; `OtherSacmNamespace`: SACM-XMI-002; `OtherRevision` and `Sacm24`: SACM-XMI-008; `EmfXmiNamespace` and `OtherXmiNamespace`: SACM-XMI-015; `Encoding`: SACM-XML-002; `Capacity` and `Unheld`: SACM-SEC-002. `WriteError::NoRoot` is SACM-XMI-001, `UnrepresentableCharacter` is SACM-XML-003 and `Invalid` is SACM-XMI-016. `template()` returns a stable id `<CODE>/<form>` that names the English sentence form. `arguments()` returns the values the sentence is made from, as named `Argument`s (`ArgumentValue::Text`, `Count` or `Prose`, LIB-DIAG-004), in the order they first appear in the sentence. Ids, names and kinds are listed in docs/sacm/diagnostics.md and follow ADR 0030 amendment 1's semver rule (ADR 0030 amendment 3). One crate-private renderer builds the variable part of every `Display` from the template and its arguments. Every `Display`, `reason` and `shape` is byte-identical to 0.1.0's for the same input. With `serde`, `ReadError`, `WriteError` and `WriteAttribute` serialize and read back. A refusal is `{"type", "code", "template", "arguments", …its fields}`.<br>_Note: Slice 0064: the template table gains the diagnostic templates (LIB-API-018); re-check there. | LIB-API-018 | **Every diagnostic carries its template and arguments.** Every `Diagnostic` the crate emits has `template()` and `arguments()`, as LIB-API-017 defines them. Its `message` is rendered from them by the same crate-private renderer, so the two cannot drift, and is byte-identical to the 0.1.0 message for the same input. A diagnostic built with `test-support`'s `Diagnostic::new`, or read from JSON that has no template, has its code's text as its template and no arguments. Diagnostics order by the seven ADR 0011 keys, then by template, then by arguments. With `serde`, a `Diagnostic` writes `template` and `arguments` after `message` (ADR 0030 amendment 3), and 0.1.0 JSON still reads, with those defaults.<br>_Note: Library only: `sacm validate --format json` keeps its ADR 0023 shape and writes no `template` or `arguments` (LIB-CLI-002). Slice 0067: every SACM 2.3 kind and end is read; the unread-kind refusals and their templates are removed (SACM23-TERM-007, -008, SACM23-AC-002, -003); re-check there. Slice 0070: arguments read in any key order (LIB-API-019); re-check there. Slice 0068: cross-document references (SACM23-XMI-027) count as values of their end and are never SACM-REF findings; the modularity rules (SACM23-VAL-013 to -015, -023) are live; re-check there. Slice 0072: read limits (LIB-SEC-003), other SACM namespaces (LIB-COMPAT-004) and ISO-8859-1 (LIB-COMPAT-016); re-check there. Slice 0073a: XMI metadata (SACM23-XMI-019, ADR 0042) and same-file proxies (SACM23-XMI-030) are read; re-check there. | LIB-EDIT-019 | **Deleting a package an interface implements or a binding binds.** Under `DeleteReferencingRelationships` and `ScrubReferences`, a dangling id in an interface's `implements` or a binding's `participantPackage` is scrubbed. An interface or binding that loses an id there and is left below the end's lower bound (no `implements`; fewer than two distinct participants, distinct ids and distinct cross-document `href`s counted, SACM23-XMI-027) is deleted with its contents, and the fixpoint continues from it. The package policy guards that holder: under `RejectIfNonEmpty` one that contains an element other than a UtilityElement, or a preserved child element, refuses the delete as `EditError::NotEmpty` naming it (SACM-CMD-006), checked after the dangling references. A holder below its bound that loses no id is untouched. | SACM23-XMI-027 | **Cross-document references.** In both modes `xmi::read` reads a reference element (production 2c) of every element reference end (each `ReferenceEnd` except the derived `expression`) whose `href`, trimmed of XML white space, has the form `document#fragment`: a non-empty document part; one `#`; a non-empty fragment with no `#`, `(` or `)`; no XML white space anywhere (§7.10.2 'URI#id_value'). It is held as a `model::Href`, exactly as trimmed, in a list of the end's own beside its ids (`SacmElement::hrefs`), in document order, repeats included. It is never resolved, and no other file is opened. An `href` counts: as an occurrence of its end (SACM23-XMI-014); toward the end's bounds (distinct ids plus distinct `href`s; ADR 0039 D3, ADR 0040); never as SACM-REF-001, SACM-REF-002 or SACM-REF-003. Both saves write an end that holds an `href` in element form: its ids as `<end xmi:idref="…" />`, then its `href`s as `<end href="…" />`, after the name and texts. `semantic_compare` reports `Difference::Hrefs`. `SetReferences` and `SetReferences::clear` set the end's ids and remove its `href`s. `AddReference` and `RemoveReference` change ids only. Every bound check counts `href`s. A delete never makes an `href` dangle, and a copy keeps them. An `href` that names no element (empty, `#`, no `#`, an empty fragment, a `#` in the fragment, or XML white space inside it) keeps the whole reference element as preserved content, with SACM-XMI-003, in both modes (LIB-COMPAT-003). A token of a reference attribute is an id, never an `href`. A role element in reference form with an `href`, an `href` with a document part as an ExpressionLangString's `expression`, a fragment holding `(` or `)` (an XPointer), and `XLink` attributes are SACM23-XMI-029's. Until then a strict read refuses them as `Unsupported` with SACM-XMI-007, and a tolerant read keeps them with that code.<br>_Note: Found in slice 0042 research. C++ drops cross-document hrefs with a Warning. Moved to M5 by the maintainer (2026-11-18, Q8). The proxies, `expression` hrefs, XPointer and XLink split to SACM23-XMI-029 (ADR 0040)._ | xmi | XMI 2.5.1 formal/15-06-07 §7.10.2 (p. 23) "The value of href must be a URI reference, as defined by IETF RFC 2396: Uniform Resource Identifiers. ## M6 — Interoperability and compliance claims

Tolerant reading of the EMF dialect, older SACM revisions, ISO-8859-1 and declared foreign subclasses, with a corpus claim of five third-party files; XMI metadata, same-file proxies and cross-document links; metamodel coverage and a generated SACM XML Schema checked against ptc/22-03-13; read limits; `sacm convert`; and the four model compliance points claimed on verified evidence (slice 0074b; docs/sacm/compliance-points.md). The assurance-forge legacy dialect, ATL output, foreign container roots and SACM 2.4 are deferred.

| ID | Requirement | Kind | Source | Status | Depends on | Tests |

| SACM23-XMI-030 | **Same-file proxies of a root package.** What a proxy is. A role element of a composite that carries `xmi:idref="id"` or `href="#id"` (trimmed) is a proxy of an element of the same document (XMI 2.5.1 §7.10.1). It carries exactly one link attribute and, optionally, one type attribute (`xmi:type`, or `xsi:type` with its SACM-XMI-010). It holds only white space, comments and processing instructions. Anything else keeps it whole with SACM-XMI-003 (`element-kept`). That includes both link attributes, any identity or other attribute, and content. Resolution. After all roots are read, a proxy whose id names a root is resolved in both modes, with no diagnostic. The root becomes a child of the proxy's container, at the proxy's place among its typed children, and stops being a root. The kind of the root must be of the role's declared type and of the proxy's type, if it gives one. Chains are followed. When it is kept instead. Nothing moves, and the proxy is kept whole as preserved content of its container, with one SACM-XMI-003 at its `<` affecting the container (row SACM23-XMI-030, clause 7.10.1), in this order of checks: the id names no root: `proxy-of-no-root`; the kind does not fit: `proxy-wrong-kind`; the root holds a preserved `href` or `xmi:idref` (it would not read back as a definition once nested): `proxy-of-linked-root`; the root keeps `type` in XMI 2.5.1's namespace or `xsi:type` as preserved content, which only a root can carry (D-ROOT-NAME): `proxy-of-typed-root` (LIB-COMPAT-020); two or more proxies that pass checks 1 to 4 name the root: `proxy-shared`, for each of them; the remaining proxies form a cycle (a strongly connected component, a self-link included): `proxy-cycle`, for each proxy in it. A proxy whose type attribute names a class its role cannot hold is no proxy: it is kept as `element-kept`, like any role element of such a type. Depth. Depth is counted as resolved: a remaining root keeps its input depth, a moved root takes its proxy's depth, and everything in its tree, parts included, shifts with it. An element deeper than `max_depth` refuses the read as `ReadError::LimitExceeded` (limit `Depth`, `SACM-SEC-003/depth`), in both modes, so that the output always reads back (D-RT) and the LIB-SEC-003 write bound holds. Placement. The document's own content keeps its place among the remaining roots (`Preserved::shift`). A write writes a moved root as a child. Strictness. Strict mode reads the same as tolerant mode, with Error instead of Warning.<br>_Note: Slice 0079 (M6 close audit): a root keeping a root-only type attribute was moved and its tolerant output did not read back; LIB-COMPAT-020 adds check 4, `proxy-of-typed-root`; re-checked by verification 0079 (its tests pass unchanged)._ | xmi | XMI 2.5.1 formal/15-06-07 §7.10.1 (pp. 22-23) "Elements act as a union, where they are either a definition or a proxy. Proxies use the LinkAttribs attribute group to define the link, and contain no nested elements." "Proxies may be chained." "When following the link from a proxy, the definition of the proxy is replaced by the referenced element."; production 2c and rules 2l, 2n (pp. 62-64); D-STRICT; M6 decisions Q3 (the maintainer, 2026-11-19); ADR 0042 | `verified` | SACM23-XMI-016, SACM23-XMI-019, LIB-COMPAT-010 | `sacm23_xmi_030_a_proxy_of_a_root_moves_the_root_into_place`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_href_hash_id_is_a_same_file_proxy`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_chains_are_followed`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_cycle_keeps_each_proxy`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_proxy_of_no_root_is_kept`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_root_two_proxies_name_is_moved_by_neither`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_proxy_of_the_wrong_kind_is_kept`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_proxy_carries_only_its_link_and_type`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_document_content_keeps_its_place`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_kept_proxy_keeps_its_place_among_metadata`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_root_with_a_link_attribute_is_not_moved`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_chain_deeper_than_the_depth_limit_is_refused`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_a_spelled_proxy_is_reported_as_spelled_and_kept`<br>`sacm23_xmi_030_the_id_a_kept_proxy_names_is_never_generated` |
| SACM23-XMI-029 | **Cross-document proxies, `expression` hrefs, XPointer and type-prefixed hrefs.** (a) XPointer. An `href` whose fragment holds `(` or `)` is an XPointer. It is held as an `Href` with `is_xpointer()` true, on any reference end, an `expression` or a proxy. Its document part may be empty. (b) Type prefix (rule 2n). The type is the part before the first run of XML white space in the trimmed value. That part must be a QName, resolved in scope, that names a concrete class in the root's SACM family. The rest is the URI reference, which may hold no white space. It is held as `sacm:<Class> <URI>`, and `Href::kind()` gives the class. A type-prefixed `#id` is the id. A type that names no concrete class, an abstract class, a foreign or unbound prefix, or a URI part with white space is SACM-XMI-003. (c) Cross-file containment proxy. A role element in reference form whose `href` names an element of another document, or an XPointer, is a cross-file containment proxy. It is held in document order as a `Proxy` (its role and its `Href`) of its container, `SacmElement::proxies()`. Its type attribute, if it has one, is held as the href's type. If both are given and differ, or the type, however it is given, is not admitted by the role, it is SACM-XMI-003. It is written after the container's children. It is never resolved, and no rule counts it, but `RejectIfNonEmpty` counts it as contained. (d) Expression href. An `href` with a document part, or an XPointer, as an ExpressionLangString's `expression` is held as `LangString::expression_href()`. It counts as the expression being present. Defects. Each of these is SACM-XMI-003 in both modes: `xmi:id`, `xmi:uuid`, `xmi:label`, a type attribute, an XLink attribute or any other attribute on a reference element; `href` beside `xmi:idref` on a reference element or a proxy. Bookkeeping. `Unread::CrossDocumentHref` is removed, and the list has no `Interim` entry. Kept proxies. A diagnostic about the spelling or the `xsi:type` of a same-file proxy that is kept affects its container, never the id the proxy names (a follow-up of slice 0073a). The SACM-XMI-010 of a kept same-file proxy or of a cross-file proxy is `SACM-XMI-010/xsi-type-on-proxy`, which names the proxy's role, its container and its class (arguments `element`, `holder_class`, `holder_id`, `class`, in sentence order, ADR 0030 amendment 3); a resolved proxy's stays `SACM-XMI-010/xsi-type`, about the root.<br>_Note: Split from SACM23-XMI-027 by slice 0068 (ADR 0040). Q4 settled the 0051 note: `href` beside `xmi:idref` is SACM-XMI-003. | LIB-EDIT-020 | **Edits create and remove cross-document references.** `Href::new`. It accepts exactly the values `Href::as_str()` can give and refuses anything else with `HrefError`. Reference edits. `SetReferences::with_hrefs` sets the end's `href`s beside its ids, replacing both lists. `AddReference::new_href` appends one `Href`. `RemoveReference::new_href` removes every occurrence of one, and is `EditError::HrefNotHeld` when the end holds none. Creates. The four interface creates take `implements` as an `Href` (`root_href`, `new_href`). The four binding creates take `participantPackage` `Href`s beside their ids (`with_participant_package_hrefs`). Expressions. `LangString::with_expression_href` sets an `expression` `Href`. Bounds and checks. Bounds count distinct ids plus distinct `href`s, and an `Href` is never checked for existence or type. serde. `Href` is a JSON string, checked by `Href::new`. `SetReferences` takes `hrefs`, which defaults to empty and is written only when it is not empty. `AddReference` and `RemoveReference` take exactly one of `id` and `href`. Interface creates take exactly one of `implements` and `implements_href`. Binding creates take `participant_package_hrefs`, which defaults to empty and is written only when it is not empty. An ExpressionLangString's `expression` is an id string, `null`, or `{"href": "…"}`. | LIB-COMPAT-004 | **Other SACM revisions.** Recognised revisions. A tolerant `xmi::read` reads a root whose local name is one of the twelve package kinds, in a namespace of an older SACM revision it recognises, as SACM 2.3, with one SACM-XMI-008 Warning per root. The recognised bases are: `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/20170843`, `/20190235` and `/20210218` (2.0, 2.1, 2.2); `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/2.0`, `/2.1` and `/2.2`; `http://omg.sacm/2.0`, `/2.1` and `/2.2`; `http://SACM_ACEditor/sacm/2.1`. Each base matches alone or followed by `/` and one or more ASCII letters (a package). SACM-like namespaces. A root in any other namespace whose URI contains `sacm` in any letter case reads as SACM 2.3 with one SACM-XMI-002 Warning per root. This covers the undated `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/2.3[/Package]`. Not SACM. A root in no namespace, or in one without `sacm`, is `InvalidRoot` (SACM-XMI-001) in both modes. SACM 2.4. A root in `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/20260504` or `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/2.4` (alone or with a package) is `Unsupported` with SACM-XMI-008 in both modes, with a reason naming LIB-COMPAT-018. Strict mode. A strict read refuses an older revision and a SACM-like namespace as `Unsupported`, with SACM-XMI-008 and SACM-XMI-002, labelled `(strict mode never reads it; LIB-COMPAT-004 reads it in tolerant mode)`. Families. In a root, every URI of the root's family counts as the SACM namespace: the base, plus base/package for the recognised and undated-2.3 bases, or the exact URI otherwise. An element or type in any other namespace is SACM-XMI-003, as a foreign one is today. Mapped spellings. Only `argumentationElement` (SACM23-XMI-009, as now) and, in a root of a recognised older revision, an Event's `occurence`, read as its `date` with one SACM-XMI-008 Warning, are mapped. Everything else 2.3 does not have is preserved content. | LIB-SEC-003 | **Resource limits.** `ReadOptions::with_limits(Limits)` bounds what `xmi::read` accepts, in both modes. Input over a limit is refused with `ReadError::LimitExceeded` (SACM-SEC-003) instead of exhausting memory. The limits and defaults are: the input's size: 32 MiB; the nesting depth of elements: 256; the XML nodes the parser builds: 1,000,000, passed to roxmltree; the namespace bindings in scope at any element: 256; and, since LIB-SEC-007, the attributes of one element: 256. Depth, bindings and (LIB-SEC-007) attributes are checked by one linear scan before parsing. The same scan counts, against the node limit, the bindings in scope at every element that declares one, which roxmltree 0.21 copies. The read stops at the first breach. It counts, against the size limit and in one budget, everything it keeps besides the parsed tree: the namespace text that preserved content keeps, counted as each element or attribute is kept, and the text arguments and affected ids of every diagnostic it emits, counted where the diagnostic is emitted (the maintainer, 2026-11-20). A refusal names the limit, its value and, where known, its location. The parser's capacities that no limit covers stay `ReadError::Unsupported` with SACM-SEC-002 and no location: more than 65,535 distinct bindings in a document, 2³² attributes, or a node limit of 2³² or more. `xmi::write` has no limit; its docs state the bound on its output. The peak memory of a read at the defaults is measured and recorded.<br>_Note: The maintainer lowered the defaults on 2026-11-19 from 128 MiB and 8M nodes to 32 MiB and 1M nodes, after the builder measured about 10 GiB peak for 8M preserved nodes. | LIB-CLI-004 | **`sacm convert`.** `sacm convert <IN> -o <OUT>` reads `<IN>` tolerantly, writes it strictly to memory, reads that output back strictly, compares the two with `compare::semantic_compare`, and writes `<OUT>` only when the strict save succeeds, the output reads back with no Error, and there is no difference. Its stdout lists every read diagnostic whose severity is Warning or Error, as its `Display` line, in `Diagnostic` order; then `<IN>: converted to <OUT>`; or, on a refusal, each schema Error of `WriteError::Invalid`, then `<IN>: not converted: <WriteError>`; on a reload failure, `<IN>: not converted: the strict output does not read back: <ReadError>`, or each Error line and `<IN>: not converted: the strict output reads back with N error(s)`; on a difference, each `Difference` line and `<IN>: not converted: N difference(s)`. Exit codes: 0 converted; 1 refused, mismatched or different, with `<OUT>` neither created nor changed; 2 (on stderr) an unreadable or refused input (`sacm: <IN>: <code\|error> <message>`), an unwritable output (`sacm: <OUT>: cannot write the output: <io error>`) or invalid arguments. `-o` is required. There is no `--strict` and no `--format`. It never reports conformance; that is `validate`'s job. A root's type that names a class declared a subclass of the root's own class is read as the root's subclass; the root's class still comes from its element name (D-ROOT-NAME). A declaration never applies to a proxy, nor to an element that carries a type in both XMI namespaces, nor to a type in the root's SACM namespaces or in SACM 2.3's, and a strict read ignores every declaration. | LIB-COMPAT-019 | **A kept type attribute writes back readable, complete XMI.** A tolerant `xmi::write` writes no attribute twice on one start tag, by name or by expanded name, and binds every prefix a kept type attribute's value names. Its output is well-formed and reads back tolerantly as the same document (D-RT). (1) A type attribute that a read keeps as preserved content or as XMI metadata (`type` in XMI 2.5.1's or EMF's XMI namespace, or `xsi:type`) keeps the binding of the prefix its value, a QName, names, in both modes and with no diagnostic of its own. The holder declares that prefix, unless it is `xml`, `xmlns`, or `sacm` or `xmi` bound to SACM 2.3 or XMI 2.5.1. A prefix `sacm` or `xmi` bound to another namespace, or no prefix under a default namespace, is replaced in the value by the holder's `nsN` for that namespace. An unbound prefix is kept as written. Other preserved values are as before (LIB-COMPAT-013). (2) In tolerant mode, an element that carries `id`, `type`, `uuid` or `label` in both XMI namespaces reads XMI 2.5.1's and keeps EMF's as written (SACM-XMI-003); a `version` in both is read as the version and ignored, both of them, with one SACM-XMI-011 each (D-XMI-VERSION); an `idref` in both on a SACM element is kept as written, both of them (SACM-XMI-003). An unprefixed type value is resolved in the default namespace in scope, as XML Schema resolves a QName and as a SACM class already is (SACM23-XMI-002), also when it names a declared subclass (LIB-COMPAT-017). (3) An element that keeps a `type` in EMF's namespace or an `xsi:type`, and no type in XMI 2.5.1's, is written with its own `xmi:type`, root or child (only a root keeps an `xsi:type`). (4) `MoveElement` and `CopyElements` refuse, as `EditError::KeptRootType` (SACM-CMD-005), to make a child of an element that keeps `type` in XMI 2.5.1's namespace or `xsi:type`, which only a root can carry (D-ROOT-NAME). | SACM23-XMI-019 | **XMI document metadata.** What is read. `xmi::read` reads, in both modes and with no diagnostic, the XMI metadata. It holds it exactly as written, both write modes write it back where it stood, and `==` and `semantic_compare` compare it (ADR 0042). The metadata is: on `xmi:XMI`: the attributes XMI.xsd gives that element (`xmi:id`, `xmi:label`, `xmi:uuid`, `href`, `xmi:idref` and `xmi:type`), plus `xsi:schemaLocation` and `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`; under `xmi:XMI`: the XMI-namespace elements `documentation`, `Documentation`, `difference`, `Difference`, `Add`, `Replace`, `Delete`, `extension` and `Extension`; on a root, a child, a `name`, a `content`, `key` or `location`, or a `value`: `xmi:uuid`, `xmi:label` and the two XSI schema-location attributes; in any of these: `xmi:extension` and `xmi:Extension` elements, kept whole, their content not checked. Accessors. `SacmElement::uuid()` and `label()` give an element's own values, read-only. Not metadata. Each of these is SACM-XMI-003: any other XMI-namespace element, kept where it stands (under `xmi:XMI`, a strict read refuses it as `Unsupported`, a defect); `href` and `xmi:idref` on a root or a text part (production 2a); identity attributes and a type attribute on a reference element (production 2c, rule 4e), which keep it whole. An XMI-namespace document element other than `xmi:XMI` is `InvalidRoot`. Ids. Metadata ids are in the document's id space, held as preserved ids are. Strict save. As `WriteError::Invalid`, a strict save refuses: a metadata `xmi:id` that is not an NCName (SACM-ID-002); a token of an XMI.xsd IDREF or IDREFS attribute in metadata that names no `xmi:id` of the output (SACM-REF-001). Edits. A copy drops the `xmi:uuid` of each copied element and part. A delete removes the metadata. A move keeps it. An edit that keeps a part's `xmi:id` keeps that part's metadata. Differences are never applied. Bookkeeping. `Unread::XmiMetadata` is removed.<br>_Note: Q2 replaced the 2026-11-16 note: role elements in reference form are SACM23-XMI-030's (same file) and SACM23-XMI-029's (another file).
