| LIB-SEC-007 | **An element's attributes are limited, so a read is not quadratic in them.** `Limits::with_max_attributes` bounds the attributes of one element that `xmi::read` accepts, in both modes, by default 256, beside LIB-SEC-003's four limits. Every attribute in a start tag counts, `xml:` attributes and repeats included, except the first declaration of each prefix (`xmlns`, or `xmlns:p`), which `max_namespace_bindings` bounds; a declaration that repeats one earlier in the same start tag binds nothing new and counts. LIB-SEC-003's pre-parse scan counts them at each start tag after the depth, the bindings in scope and the namespace copies, and refuses an element over the limit with `ReadError::LimitExceeded` (SACM-SEC-003, `Limit::Attributes`, template `SACM-SEC-003/attributes`) at the `<` of its start tag, before roxmltree parses it, wherever it stands: a root, a SACM element, preserved content or the `XMI` element. roxmltree 0.21.2 compares each attribute of an element with the earlier ones, so its time per element grows with the square of that element's attributes. The limit caps this at `max_attributes - 1` comparisons per attribute, and the rest of the read, kept attributes included, is linear in them, so a read at the defaults is linear in its input. Raising the limit brings back the parser's quadratic cost for the elements that use it, and `with_max_attributes` says so. `xmi::write` has no limit: an element can be written with more attributes than it was read with (values read in element form, a generated `xmi:id`).<br>_Note: Slice 0077: the cause is roxmltree's duplicate-attribute check, quadratic per element, and the reader itself was measured linear. A limit was chosen over a fork (ADR 0041 amendment 2). When a roxmltree release makes the check linear, the default can rise; re-check then. The parser's namespace scans per element are bounded by `max_namespace_bindings`, the copy count and, for repeated declarations, which roxmltree 0.21.2 does not refuse for `xmlns` and `xmlns:xml`, `max_attributes`. Verification round 1 found the repeats (roxmltree issue 153 also names namespace declarations); LIB-SEC-008 refuses them as malformed XML after the parse, so the parse still sees them and this count is what bounds its cost; re-checked by verification 0078: LIB-SEC-008 refuses them after this scan, which still bounds the parse. | LIB-SEC-008 | **A repeated namespace declaration is malformed XML.** `xmi::read` refuses, in both modes, a start tag that declares the same prefix twice (`xmlns` twice, or `xmlns:p` twice for any `p`, `xml` included) as `ReadError::Malformed` (SACM-XML-001), at the first character of the name of the first repeat. roxmltree 0.21.2 refuses a repeated `xmlns:p` for an ordinary `p` (`SACM-XML-001/duplicate-prefix`), and a repeat whose value it refuses anyway, but it accepts a repeated `xmlns` or `xmlns:xml`. The check runs among those checks, earliest offending construct first: after the pre-parse limits scan (an element over a limit is `LimitExceeded`, whatever it repeats) and roxmltree's own refusals, and before any root is classified. Within an attribute it comes after the empty-prefix and `xmlns:xmlns` checks of the name and before the checks of the value. Each declaration is compared with the earlier ones of its start tag in constant time. Only the same name in one start tag is refused. The same prefix on another element, two prefixes bound to one namespace, `XMLNS`, and the text of a comment, CDATA section, processing instruction or attribute value are not.<br>_Note: Filed in slice 0077 (2026-11-25), pre-existing. Slice 0078: refused among LIB-SEC-005's checks after the parse, not in the pre-parse scan, so the earliest offending construct is still the one reported and the scan refuses only limits. The parser still parses the repeats before they are refused; LIB-SEC-007 counts them, which keeps that parse bounded. ## M7 — 1.0 candidate, released as 0.5.0

The API and docs meant for 1.0, released as 0.5.0 so consumers can try them before 1.0 freezes them: the breaking changes and additions Assurance Forge asked for (lasrod/libSACM#113), a public API review, short and structured documentation everywhere with a user guide and primer, property tests, fuzzing, coverage and semver checks (the maintainer, 2026-11-26).
